rationale:
Evidence: iteration 1 (16 mm sensors at x ±0.03, kp 3.5, kd 0.6) scored 232.9, slightly below the baseline's 238.3. Line-loss events on the s-bend fell from 2.05 to 1.15 and on the slalom from 1.75 to 1.05, so wider coverage helped. The oval finish rate dropped from 0.40 to 0.35 and oval steering_oscillation rose from 0.24 to 0.29. The s-bend max_error stayed at about 0.063, above the 0.06 m limit, so the robot still drifts out on bends. Completion has only come from the oval, and the 500-point completion bonus dominates the score.

Changes: (1) Sensor y moves from 0.04 to 0.06 m ahead of the axle. Readings then lead the wheels by more, which reduces the phase lag that lets bend error build up. (2) Mass drops from 0.8 to 0.6 kg. Yaw inertia scales with mass, so the robot turns more readily and drifts less on bends. (3) kp drops from 3.5 to 3.0 and kd rises from 0.6 to 0.7, to cut the oval oscillation seen in iteration 1 while keeping bend tracking. (4) base_speed drops from 1.5 to 1.4. Line losses are still about 1 per run on bends, and the reviewer's rule says to reduce speed when losses stay high. The oval mean finish of 1.93 s at 1.5 leaves some margin for 1.4. Sensor x-spacing, sensor size, wheel geometry, ki, sensor_weights and line_loss are unchanged.

Expected result: fewer line losses on the s-bend and slalom (target below 0.8 per run), s-bend max_error below 0.06, oval steering_oscillation near 0.25, and the oval finish rate at or above the baseline's 0.40. Hypotheses to test: (a) the forward sensor shift and lower mass reduce bend drift; (b) the 1.4 base_speed keeps the oval finish within 3 s. If the s-bend still ends off track with max_error above 0.06, the next step is a larger kd or a lower base_speed of about 1.3. If the oval finish drops, return base_speed to 1.5 with these gains.
